newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices soar on good sentiment.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices soar on good sentiment.

text.p: China's A and B share indices continued their upward trend to close sharply higher on Wednesday on positive sentiment following gains in the past few days, brokers said.
Shanghai's B share index rose 1.87 percent to 71.619 points on turnover of $15.6 million, up from Tuesday's $11 million.
Shenzhen's B share index soared 3.09 percent to 162.2 points as turnover expanded to HK$146.2 million ($18.86 million) from HK$95 million on Tuesday.

On the Shanghai B share market, follow-up buying emerged after the B index rose above the 68 to 69-point resistance level on Tuesday. The strong performance of A shares also boosted domestic investors' confidence, brokers said.
Shanghai's A share index ended at 1,177.703 points, up 1.47 percent with turnover hitting 9.7 billion yuan ($1.17 billion), up from 8.7 billion yuan on Tuesday.

Shanghai brokers said the indices were likely to rise further in the short term, but potential was limited because the markets had been supported by a speculative mood which may trigger intervention from Beijing to cool them.
On both Shanghai's A and B share markets, Shanghai Vacuum & Electron Device Co was the star on domestic buying triggered by talk of an upcoming financial restructuring, brokers said.
Its B share soared 9.52 percent to $0.23, while its A share surged to its 10 percent limit-up of 6.67 yuan.
A company official confirmed the report after the close.
Textile company Shanghai Worldbest Co was the most active B share on expectations of good 1996 results, rising $0.014 or 2.8 percent to $0.514 on volume of 2.9 million shares.
Shenzhen's B share index rose sharply helped by Wuxi Little Swan Co Ltd which surged after it announced a plan to offer 51 million A shares, broker said.
The issue closed at HK$10.48, up HK$0.95 or 9.97 percent on volume of 818,900 shares.
The day's rise was also linked to the Shenzhen Expressway Co which posted a strong debut on the Hong Kong exchange on Wednesday, brokers said.
The road company closed at HK$2.775 against its offer price of HK$2.20.

Institutional buying in index-weighted issues such as Changan Automobile also contributed to the index's advance, analysts said. Changan traded most on turnover of HK$9.1 million, rising HK$0.22 to HK$4.78.
Shenzhen's A share index maintained its upward trend to close up 1.01 percent at 414.13 points, with investors continuing to put money into issues expected to post solid 1996 results, brokers said.
Turnover was a weighty 10.98 billion yuan compared with Tuesday's 9.34 billion yuan.
